chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Isma'il ibn Jabr said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who confessed to one of his heirs that he had a debt upon himself while he was ill. He said: 'It is valid for him if he confesses to it for less than one-third.'

key_terms.إِقْرَار: Confession or acknowledgment of a debt or right
key_terms.الثُّلُث: One-third, a key fraction in Islamic inheritance and wills
key_terms.مَرِيضٌ: A person who is ill, specifically in the context of deathbed illness

ai.seo_question: What is the validity of a dying person's confession of debt to an heir in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a dying person's confession of debt to an heir is legally valid provided it does not exceed one-third of the estate, mirroring the standard limit for wills (*wasiyya*). This ruling prevents the potential for self-dealing or unfair depletion of the remaining heirs' shares, ensuring that the testator's acknowledgment of debt is treated with the same caution as a voluntary bequest. The limitation to one-third safeguards the rights of other heirs while respecting the deceased's right to settle obligations before distribution.
